claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys contain pronounced nanoscale chemical inhomogeneities.
As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys contain residual internal strain fields.
Nanoscale chemical inhomogeneities act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Local strain fields act as pinning centers for magnetic domains or domain walls and thereby increase coercivity and hysteretic loss.
Domain-wall pinning caused by chemical and strain heterogeneity produces a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type material has a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with significant hysteresis.
A sufficiently mild, low-temperature, time-controlled anneal will reduce nanoscale chemical inhomogeneity.
A sufficiently mild, low-temperature, time-controlled anneal will relax local internal strain.
Within the proposed annealing window, the primary phase and overall composition will remain unchanged.
Thermal processing outside a suitable parameter window can cause substantial grain growth or phase transformation.
Reducing local strain and chemical heterogeneity will reduce magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Reduced domain-wall pinning will make the magnetostructural transition more gradual and less hysteretic.
Annealed samples will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will retain a similar entropy-change magnitude to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will have lower coercivity than the as-deposited baseline.
The reduced hysteresis will improve magnetic-cooling-cycle performance under low applied fields.
The predictions apply across the FeMnNiGeSi alloy family provided that annealing does not trigger phase transformation or significant grain coarsening.
XRD peak FWHM can jointly indicate nanoscale strain relaxation and improved chemical homogeneity in these samples.
